tests.name: equality-comparison
tests.description: The Equality and Comparison operator sections: =, ~, != and !~ over Boolean, Integer, Decimal, String, Date, DateTime, Time, Quantity and complex types, with empty operands, operands of several items, precision and timezone offsets; the comparison operators >, <, <= and >= over the types they are defined on; and what FHIR's FHIRPath pages (R4, R5) add: FHIR primitives compared as System types, the FHIR Quantity mapping, and Coding/CodeableConcept equivalence. Where 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 differ the cases follow 2.0.0 (whitespace set for string equivalence, calendar day/hour/minute/week against UCUM units) and cite both texts; where 2.0.0's own examples contradict its definitions (<= and >=) the cases follow the definitions and the corrected 3.0.0 examples. Unit conversion is optional in both versions, so cases that involve two different units only exclude the wrong Boolean and accept empty; ~ between commensurable units is written only where the most granular (2.0.0) and least granular (3.0.0) unit give the same answer. Leaves out what the text does not settle: = between one item and several (the text says both false and error), = or ~ between items of types with no implicit conversion, Date against DateTime, DateTime with and without an offset, ordering of partial dates whose earlier components already differ, comparison of Booleans, comparison of an empty operand with one of several items, incommensurable or invalid units, ~ between commensurable units where the unit it converts to changes the answer, rounding ties in decimal equivalence, ~ over collections with duplicates, = over several items where no pair is false and some pair is empty, FHIR equivalence ignoring element ids (no official input has element ids), and the order of a union.

group.name: REQ-EQUALITYCOMPARISON-001
group.description: = and != return empty when either operand is empty, including when both are
group.source: Like functions, operators will generally propagate an empty collection in any of their operands. This is true even when comparing two empty collections using the equality operators, e.g.
{} != 'dummy'
all result in `{}`.
If one or both of the operands is the empty collection, this operation returns an empty collection.
The converse of the equals operator, returning `true` if equal returns `false`; `false` if equal returns `true`; and empty (`{ }`) if equal returns empty.
{} = {} // empty ; as explicitly defined above

This means that when, in an underlying data object (i.e. they physical data on which the implementation is operating) a member is null or missing, there will simply be no corresponding node for that member in the tree, e.g. `Patient.name` will return an empty collection (not null) if there are no name elements in the instance.

group.name: REQ-EQUALITYCOMPARISON-006
group.description: = over Date, DateTime and Time compares precision by precision: a differing value gives false, a precision only one side has gives empty, and the end of both gives true
group.source: For `Date`, `DateTime` and `Time` equality, the comparison is performed by considering each precision in order, beginning with years (or hours for time values), and respecting timezone offsets.

If the values are the same, comparison proceeds to the next precision; if the values are different, the comparison stops and the result is `false`. If one input has a value for the precision and the other does not, the comparison stops and the result is empty (`{ }`); if neither input has a value for the precision, or the last precision has been reached, the comparison stops and the result is `true`.

If the values are the same, comparison proceeds to the next precision; if the values are different, the comparison stops and the result is `false`. If one input has a value for the precision and the other does not, the comparison stops and the result is empty (`{ }`); if neither input has a value for the precision, or the last precision has been reached, the comparison stops and the result is `true`.

@2012 = @2013 // returns false

group.name: REQ-EQUALITYCOMPARISON-017
group.description: ~ over Strings ignores case and treats each whitespace character as equivalent to any other, without collapsing or trimming
group.source: `String`: the strings must be the same, ignoring case and locale, and normalizing whitespace (see <<string-equivalence>> for more details).

For strings, equivalence returns true if the strings are the same value while ignoring case and locale, and normalizing whitespace. Normalizing whitespace means that all whitespace characters are treated as equivalent, with whitespace characters as defined in the <<whitespace, Whitespace>> lexical category.
FHIRPath defines _tab_ (`\t`), _space_ (`` ``), _line feed_ (`\n`) and _carriage return_ (`\r`) as _whitespace_, meaning they are only used to separate other tokens within the language.
For strings, equivalence returns `true` if the strings are the same value while ignoring case and locale, and normalizing whitespace.
Multiple whitespace characters in sequence are not collapsed to a single character.
To simply trim the start and end of content, use the [`trim()`](#trim--string) function.
'a' ~ 'A' // true ; case is ignored for equivalence
'a b' ~ 'a\tb' // true
'a b' ~ 'a b' // false ; the whitespace isn't collapsed
'a b' ~ 'A B' // true ; case insensitive test

group.name: REQ-EQUALITYCOMPARISON-036
group.description: Quantities of different but commensurable units are compared after conversion where the implementation converts, and otherwise may give empty, but never the wrong Boolean
group.source: When comparing quantities, the dimensions of each quantity must be the same, but not necessarily the unit. For example, units of 'cm' and 'm' can be compared, but units of 'cm2' and 'cm' cannot. The comparison will be made using the most granular unit of either input.

group.name: REQ-EQUALITYCOMPARISON-045
group.description: ~ over Quantities of different but commensurable units compares them after conversion where the implementation converts, and otherwise may give empty, but never the wrong Boolean; the cases are chosen so that 2.0.0 (most granular unit) and 3.0.0 (least granular unit) give the same answer
group.source: When comparing quantities for equivalence, the dimensions of each quantity must be the same, but not necessarily the unit. For example, units of 'cm' and 'm' can be compared, but units of 'cm2' and 'cm' cannot. The comparison will be made using the most granular unit of either input.
Implementations are not required to fully support operations on units, but they must at least respect units, recognizing when units differ.
Implementations that do not support complete UCUM functionality may return empty (`{ }`) for calculations involving quantities with units where the units are different.
When the units are different the quantity values must be [**converted**](#unit-conversions) to the least granular unit before comparison.

Once the units are the same, the values can be compared using decimal equivalence: values must be equal, comparison is done on values rounded to the precision of the least precise operand. Trailing zeroes after the decimal are ignored in determining precision (as described above).
2.1 'cm' ~ 21 'mm' // true ; convert to least granular 'cm' (2.1 ~ 2.1), round to least precise and compare (2.1 = 2.1)
4 'g' ~ 4000 'mg' // true ; convert to least granular 'g' (4 ~ 4.000), round to least precise and compare (4 = 4)
The converse of the equivalent operator, returning `true` if equivalent returns `false` and `false` is equivalent returns `true`. In other words, `A !~ B` is short-hand for `(A ~ B).not()`.
